source.title: Bad Global Minima Exist and SGD Can Reach Them
source.authors: Sheng-Chao Liu; Dimitris Papailiopoulos; D. Achlioptas

record.file_problem: Text is the full paper; no obvious truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how training after random-label pretraining affects later generalization, and finds that vanilla SGD reaches poor-generalizing perfect fits while regularized training mitigates the effect. It refines the claim by showing that successful fitting of random labels does not imply the later true-label fit generalizes well.
record.gate_note: The paper's random-label pretraining is an initialization procedure, not a direct evaluation of random-label test error. Rows below cover separately reported training/test accuracies for the resulting adversarial initialization and controls. The cited Zhang et al. random-label result is prior work and is not recorded as a result of this study. Figure-only trajectories and numerous per-model/per-dataset results are not transcribed where aggregate statements or Table 2 give the reported outcome.
record.test_reason: The paper reports successful random-label fitting during construction of adversarial initializations, including an explicit 100% fit in its toy experiment. It also tests the role of regularization in true-label generalization under random and pretrained initializations. Its main downstream results do not measure random-label fitting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: random-label pretraining can make vanilla SGD reach true-label fits with poor generalization, while augmentation, L2 regularization and momentum help escape that initialization. The authors emphasize regularization's role in search dynamics. Individual heuristics do not uniformly restore the corresponding random-initialization accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than directly testing the original random-label fit and chance test error, the study uses random-label training to construct adversarial initializations, then measures subsequent true-label training. It tests vanilla SGD and regularized/augmented variants across image datasets and architectures.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on initialization (random versus adversarial), training heuristics (data augmentation, L2 regularization, momentum), replication factor R, dataset and architecture. The paper notes that nonstandard adaptive or very large learning-rate schedules could also alter escape, but uses standard decaying schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: Following random-label pretraining, models usually fit true labels perfectly but can generalize substantially worse than models trained from random initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label pretraining can steer subsequent vanilla SGD toward poorly generalizing true-label interpolating solutions.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding training heuristics reduces or eliminates the downstream effect of adversarial initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Augmentation, L2 regularization and momentum affect recovery from random-label pretraining; combinations generally recover comparable test performance.

record.problems: The study does not directly report random-label test error or time to fit random labels; much of the multi-model/multi-dataset evidence is presented in figures, while numerical uncertainty is shown for the ResNet18 CIFAR10 heuristic comparison. DenseNet falls slightly below 100% training accuracy in some settings.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports separate figure trajectories for each model and dataset in Figures 2–4 and appendices Figures 7–22; not all individual figure-only values were extracted. Retained aggregate text statements and all Table 2 ResNet18 CIFAR10 heuristic comparisons, which include the informative single-heuristic and combined-heuristic outcomes.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error on the random-label task is not measured. Architecture-specific random-label training accuracies and matched fitting protocols are not comprehensively reported; Algorithm 1 allows training until convergence when perfect fitting fails.
No measured comparison of random-label versus true-label fitting time or convergence across corruption fractions. The introductory timing statement cites prior work.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or unstructured Gaussian-noise input fitting experiments. The toy Gaussian clusters retain class structure.
No sweep over label-corruption fractions with corresponding training and test errors.

No random-label fitting experiment with weight decay, dropout, or augmentation applied as the tested regularization intervention. Dropout is not tested. Pixel zeroing during initializer construction is not a controlled test of this component.
No within-training measurement of learning real patterns before memorizing noisy labels. Sequentially training on random and then true labels does not test that ordering.

missing.what: The toy experiment explicitly achieves 100% random-label training accuracy in Setting 2. Record this separately from subsequent true-label fitting.
missing.locator: Section 1, A Sketch of the Phenomenon; Figure 1b

missing.what: Section 3.3 reports models achieving 100% random-label accuracy when constructing adversarial initializers. Capture this textual result with Algorithm 1's caveat that some architectures instead train until convergence; do not infer perfect random-label fitting for every architecture.
missing.locator: Section 3.3, paragraph discussing distance from random initialization to the random-label model; Algorithm 1 and footnote 4

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 verdicts incorrectly use subsequent true-label outcomes as random-label-fitting evidence. The study does not challenge random-label memorization. V5 verdicts concern its true-label generalization component only; downstream recovery cannot establish that regularizers fail to prevent random-label fitting.

versions.untested_parts: The study trains adversarial initializers on random labels, but does not report their test error at chance or directly compare random-label fitting time with true-label fitting time.
No comparison of time to fit random versus true labels or convergence time as label corruption varies.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
No sweep over fractions of corrupted labels or test-error curve from none to all.
Tests whether regularization and augmentation mitigate the effect of random-label pretraining; does not test dropout or whether removing regularization alone makes true-label generalization poor.
No measurement of which labels are learned first during training.

relation.reason: Its own experiments measure random-label fitting and true-label generalization across regularization and initialization conditions.

tranche.reason: The study directly qualifies V5: random-label pretraining creates an initialization under which removing explicit regularization substantially worsens true-label generalization.

source_check.notes: The V5 comparisons concern true-label training; they do not test whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting. Algorithm 1's footnote allows training to convergence when an architecture cannot reach perfect random-label accuracy.
